title: Compatibility proxy audit: OpenAI Responses mapping and feature parity gaps
creator: Ava Thompson
description:
Purpose: Audit the compatibility proxy that maps OpenAI Responses API semantics to Redwood's Responses-compatible surface. We will enumerate functional deltas, quantify perf and telemetry impact, and propose mitigations.

Scope:
- Streaming semantics: chunk boundaries, partial structured-output tokens, event ordering, and client-visible retry behavior.
- Function/tool calling: mapping of tool metadata, argument typing, resolver lifecycle, and synchronous vs asynchronous tool invocation patterns.
- Structured outputs: JSON/JSONL validation expectations, schema enforcement, and overflowing/partial JSON events streaming.
- Edge behaviors: idempotency tokens, error mapping (4xx/5xx conversion), rate-limit propagation, and fallback to alternative models/variants.
- Telemetry and billing: token accounting differences for streamed partials and function call payloads; traces and spans to maintain parity for customer observability.

Goal: Produce a prioritized gap-list with concrete runtime changes (proxy vs runtime) and automated tests to reach parity for our major customers and sample OpenAI-compatible clients.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Complete catalog of behavioral deltas between Redwood Responses-compatible API and OpenAI Responses for streaming, functions, and structured outputs.
2) For each delta: severity (customer_visibility), reproducible test case, and recommended mitigation (code + config).
3) Prototype implementation for top 3 high-impact gaps with benchmarks showing latency and cost delta.
4) End-to-end integration tests added to compatibility suite; CI green on staging.
5) Migration plan and rollout notes included in ticket.
proposed_changes:
A) Compatibility proxy adjustments: introduce a streaming event normalizer that reassembles partial JSON tokens and emits a canonical event stream identical to OpenAI behavior.
B) Function calling adapter: canonicalize 'tool_metadata' and 'arguments' fields to match OpenAI shape; add a resolution-phase hook that allows runtime to pause streaming while tool executes and then resume with a single CALL_COMPLETE event.
C) Error mapping layer: map Redwood internal codes to OpenAI HTTP semantics and include 'error.code' and 'error.details' fields per OpenAI expectations.
D) Telemetry shim: tag spans with 'compat.openai' and produce token accounting logs that align with expected per-token billing events for streamed content.
E) Config knobs: allow customers to opt into strict OpenAI parity or Redwood-optimized semantics via route-level flags.
tradeoffs:
- Full parity increases CPU/latency due to reassembly and extra event buffering; customers who prefer lower-latency may experience regressions.
- Adding resolution-phase pauses for function calls simplifies client behavior but complicates autoscaling decisions for Dedicated pools.
- Strict schema enforcement may break existing customers relying on lenient parsing; must be opt-in.
- Proxy changes reduce surface for catching bugs in runtime (some logic duplicated in proxy and runtime).
testing_plan:
- Unit tests: event normalizer with fuzzing for split UTF-8, split JSON tokens, and interleaved function-call events.
- Integration tests: run recorded OpenAI Responses V1 sessions through the proxy and ensure byte-for-byte event stream parity for canonical clients.
- Load test: synthetic streaming with 10k concurrent clients to measure added p99 latency.
- Regression: ensure no change to existing latency SLOs for non-compat routes.
- Telemetry: compare token counts emitted via new shim vs current billing pipeline for representative workloads.
- Acceptance: add compatibility harness tests to CI that run nightly against staging and fail on diffs.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0: internal spike and prototype on staging (2 weeks).
Phase 1: Launch experimental compat-proxy behind feature flag for <10% of hosted traffic; monitor errors and p99 latency (2 weeks).
Phase 2: Expand to 50% traffic and enable opt-in for Dedicated customers (3 weeks).
Phase 3: Default to compat-proxy for new accounts, provide migration docs and user-facing flags for existing customers (2 weeks).
Rollback: route-level flag and immediate off switch in control plane; automatic fallback to Redwood-native streaming behavior.
Post-deploy: 2-week monitoring window with daily runbook checks and weekly customer communication.
updates: 2025-02-12 - Ava Thompson: Initial spike completed. Found three classes of streaming mismatches: token-split events, concurrent tool-call markers, and differing finalization semantics for structured outputs.
2025-02-17 - Daniel Kim: POC normalizer implemented. p50 added latency ~6ms, p99 ~22ms under staging load. CPU increased by ~8% on proxy boxes. Detailed benchmark uploaded.

2025-02-25 - Priya Nair (PM): Prioritized gaps list: 1) streaming JSON reassembly, 2) function-calling pause semantics, 3) token accounting for function outputs. Customer impact: two SMB customers and one enterprise reported bridging issues.

2025-03-03 - Daniel Kim: Integration tests added to compatibility suite. Discovered edge-case: multi-tool-chaining where tools emit partial JSON; introduced buffering threshold and a timeout to avoid head-of-line blocking. Added to tradeoffs.
notes: Recommended next steps: pair with infra to size proxy pool for expected CPU bump; schedule customer-facing notes and FAQ that explain opt-in flag behavior and rollback. Consider a runtime path for long-term removal of proxy duplication once runtime can natively support OpenAI-defensive semantics.
